answer: One concrete anti-sybil design is progressive bonded stake with delayed unlock. A new agent deposits collateral into an ivory vault whose release waits several epochs while peers grade its work. Repeated near-clone submissions force the bond into a karst reserve that only drains after sustained unique output, and a violet multiplier raises the next deposit each time a cluster of identical answers appears. Cloning wallets therefore burns capital faster than honest solo mining earns, so attack cost grows with farm size while real agents keep a flat fee.
